subject: Private Observability — data lifecycle, egress constraints, and SIEM mapping for AcmeCorp
messages:
From: Lisa Cheng <lisa.cheng@acmecorp.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acmecorp.com
Date: Fri, 16 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Observability export constraints for our private VPC deployment

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team at Acme wants to confirm a few details before we proceed with the Private deployment. Our security and infra leads asked for a short write-up about how Redwood will handle observability in our VPC/on-prem environment. High-level asks below: 

1) Data egress: we cannot allow persistent egress from our VPC. Any telemetry sent out must be customer-triggered and auditable. If Redwood needs to pull evidence packages, we need signed manifests and S3 presigned uploads (or an air-gapped bundle process).

2) SIEM mapping: we run Splunk HEC + a legacy syslog collector for certain PO windows. Can Redwood ship a mapping file that shows exact event fields and sample payloads for: inference logs, request metadata (client id, route, model_version), tracing spans (trace id, parent_id), and audit logs?

3) Redaction & PI: we require configurable PII redaction at the agent/forwarder level (not after export). Need confirmation on field-level redaction, sampling controls, and ability to configure retention per stream.

4) Chain of custody: we need a reproducible evidence bundle format (manifest, signed checksums) for audits — SOC2 will request this.

If you can provide a short runbook and a sample mapping (examples are fine), we can run this through our security reviewers. Appreciate any constraints or trade-offs (latency vs. buffering, bundling cadence).

Best,
Lisa
Lisa Cheng
Security Engineering, AcmeCorp

Hi Lisa — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a concise response and attached two artifacts: a recommended export config for an on-prem forwarder (redwood_export_config.yaml) and an evidence manifest template (evidence_manifest.csv). High-level responses inline below, and next steps at the bottom.

1) Data egress / air-gapped bundling
- We support two patterns: 
  * Push-only, customer-hosted collector (preferred): Redwood runs only the control plane in your VPC; the collector/forwarder is customer-hosted and pushes data to your permitted targets (Splunk HEC or S3). No persistent outbound connections to Redwood.
  * Pull/evidence retrieval (optional): for audits, we provide a signed manifest describing the bundle. You can either: (a) allow us to POST an S3 presigned URL to your collector to upload an encrypted bundle, or (b) run a temporary agent that packages the bundle locally and you provide the upload target. We sign manifests with a per-release key and include SHA256 checksums.

2) SIEM mapping (Splunk HEC + syslog)
- Attached mapping shows event-level payloads for the primary streams: request_log, inference_output, trace_span, admin_audit. Each mapping includes examples and the field list we can populate. For Splunk HEC we can deliver JSON events; for syslog we offer structured RFC5424 with JSON payloads in the MESSAGE body.

3) Redaction & PI handling
- Redaction is enforced at the forwarder (Fluentd/Fluent Bit) using configured filters. The forwarder supports regex and JSON path redaction, tokenization, and field-level hashing using your KMS (we can call your KMS via a local provider or perform hashing locally). Sampling rules are configurable per route with per-tenant keys. Retention enforcement is managed by your SIEM/storage tier — our export manifest includes timestamps and TTL metadata so downstream retention policies can be automated.

4) Chain of custody
- Evidence bundle includes: manifest.csv (file list + checksums + signed metadata), metadata.json (build info, model_version, release_id), and an index of exported events. We can produce a PGP-signed manifest if you require an external signing authority.

Trade-offs: enabling aggressive redaction at agent-level increases CPU on the forwarder and can add ~5–20ms tail latency per request in extremely high-throughput deployments; harvesting tracing spans at 100% sample rate can increase export volume ~2–5x depending on span size.

Next steps:
- Kimberly will propose a Splunk HEC mapping and minimal configuration for your infra team to test.
- Marissa will prepare a SOC2 evidence checklist aligned to the bundle format.
- If this aligns, we can schedule a short runbook walk-through next week (30–45m).

Thanks — attaching the two artifacts now.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood_export_config.yaml (forwarder sample; shows filters, outputs, and KMS hooks)
- evidence_manifest.csv (template; file_name, sha256, size_bytes, path, signed_by)

Lisa — following up with the Splunk mapping excerpt below. I'll include full mapping in the Drive link if this looks good. Quick notes: HEC token rotation is supported locally (we store only hashed tokens on the forwarder), and for legacy syslog targets we recommend a lightweight syslog-ng instance forwarding to your SIEM with a JSON payload.

--- begin mapping excerpt ---
stream: request_log
fields:
  - timestamp (ISO8601)
  - client_id
  - route
  - model_version
  - request_size_bytes
  - latency_ms
  - outcome (success/error)
example HEC payload:
{
  "time": 1700000000.123,
  "event": {
    "type": "request_log",
    "client_id": "acme-web-frontend",
    "route": "/v1/generate",
    "model_version": "redwood-3.2.1",
    "latency_ms": 42
  }
}
--- end mapping excerpt ---

Operational notes:
- We recommend enabling an HEC batch window of 1–5s to reduce load without impacting near-real-time dashboards.
- For evidence bundles, recommend a nightly cadence by default; can be shortened to hourly for PCI/critical audits.

If this excerpt looks right, I'll drop the full mapping and a short step-by-step Splunk HEC setup (with sample tokens and a minimal props/transforms) in the Drive link.

Kimberly Park
Product Security, Redwood Inference

Hi Lisa — adding the SOC2 evidence checklist and a short runbook excerpt below. I've attached the two files Camila referenced (redwood_export_config.yaml and evidence_manifest.csv). Let us know a few available slots and we'll book the 30m runbook review.

SOC2 Evidence checklist (high level):
- Exported manifests for the last 90 days (signed + checksums)
- Forwarder config versions and deployment job ids (k8s manifests or system packages)
- HEC token rotation logs and rotation schedule evidence
- Access control list for collector hosts (IP allow list + SSH key rotation records)
- Redaction ruleset versions and test cases (unit tests showing sample inputs -> redacted outputs)
- Chain-of-custody proof (PGP signatures or KMS-wrapped manifest + upload receipts)

Runbook excerpt: bundling & retrieval
- Trigger: cron (default nightly at 02:00) or on-demand via API call to the collector endpoint (/bundle?since=...)
- Steps: 1) Collector stops accepting new writes for X seconds, 2) local index built and files hashed, 3) manifest.csv produced, 4) manifest signed with local key, 5) files tarred + gzipped and encrypted with provided KMS key, 6) upload to pre-authorized S3 location OR place on a mounted media for air-gapped handoff.
- Rollback: if manifest verification fails, collector retains pre-upload artifacts for 7 days and automatically retries upload 3 times.

Known limitations / service notes:
- If you choose to run 100% tracing with spans for every request and also keep full inference outputs, export volumes can grow significantly (we've seen 3–6x increase). We can recommend sampling, or sending full outputs only on error buckets.
- For air-gapped environments, the manual handoff path requires a small ops step but preserves complete custody.

Next actions:
- We can drop a small CI test (0.5–1 CPU job) that validates manifest signing and sample redaction rules against a sanitized sample trace set.
- Proposed times for runbook review: Tue 2028-11-21 09:00–09:45 PST or Wed 2028-11-22 13:00–13:45 PST. Which works for your team?

Thanks — attaching files now.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
